svg.title: A Codex session as a durable workflow
svg.desc: The workflow holds the thread, the sandbox handle, and the snapshot id. Model calls, shell commands, and snapshots are activities. The sandbox is a separate machine.
svg.text: Thread items: instructions, the login-form request, tool calls, tool results.
Sandbox handle: how to reconnect to the live room.
Snapshot id: files to seed a fresh room when the live one is gone.
The workflow waits here for your next message. That wait survives a worker restart.
An approval is the same kind of wait: the shell stays un-run until your signal arrives.
Replay returns every finished activity's recorded result and continues at the open one.
The model credential stays on the worker that runs the model activity.
It checks in while the tests run.
A retry checks the call id
The login-form repo, the compilers, and the secrets the tests read.
Session state reconnects to this machine. A snapshot seeds a new one.
Those are different records. The workflow remembers which one is current.
A full test log stays in a file here. The activity result keeps a bounded copy.
OpenAI's sandbox guide names the same three surfaces: run state for the harness,
session state for the live room, and a snapshot for a fresh room.
Temporal's history is the place that holds them across a worker crash.
Local Codex already stores a thread on disk. This layout stores it outside both the process and the room.
